title: Compare against the original Go beads and decide what to port
description:
Run one comparison round against the original Go `beads` (binary `bd`), reading
a local checkout supplied at execution time, and decide feature by feature what
is worth porting into this fork. Produce a decision document, not code.

This fork descends from `Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust`, a Rust port of the Go
original. The port is not complete, and the Go project has kept moving since it
was made — so this fork is missing two distinct things that need separating:
features the Rust port never carried, and features the Go project added
afterwards. This task tells them apart and picks the ones that matter.

## Baseline measured 2026-07-30

Go original (HEAD `750fd5741`, dated 2026-07-30 — actively
developed, merging PRs the same day):
- 1,881 `.go` files, ~573k lines.
- **191 distinct command tokens** registered via cobra `Use:` across
  `cmd/bd/*.go` (top-level plus subcommands).

This fork:
- **24 top-level commands** (plus `help`): blocked, close, comments, completions, config,
  create, delete, dep, epic, history, info, init, label, list, ready, reopen,
  search, show, stale, stats, status, sync, update, version (+ help).

The gap is not a to-do list. Much of the Go surface is deliberately out of scope
here: the Dolt storage backend, federation and peers, replicas and leases,
swarm/claim pools, db-proxy/server modes, and the issue-tracker bridges (jira,
linear, github, gitlab, notion, ado). The fork's whole premise is a local,
single-user, SQLite+JSONL tracker. Do not port scope back in by accident.

## What the round must produce

A written comparison, stored as an attachment on the epic this task spawns,
covering:

1. **A three-way classification of the Go command surface.** For each command:
   present here / absent-and-wanted / absent-and-deliberately-out-of-scope.
   State the reason for every out-of-scope call — "single-user local tracker"
   is a valid reason, "looks complicated" is not.

2. **The behaviour gaps inside commands we already have.** This is where the
   real value is, and a command-name diff will miss it entirely. Compare flags,
   output shape, and semantics for the 24 commands above — `bd show` vs
   `br show`, `bd list` filters vs `br list`, `bd sync` vs `br sync`,
   `bd epic` vs `br epic`. Note `bds-04l.9` already records that `br show`
   drops 9 fields in Rich mode; expect more of that class.

3. **Data-model deltas.** The Go `types.Issue` has fields this fork's `Issue`
   does not (the CHANGELOG's `LeaseGrantedNode` is one example, and it rides the
   JSONL interchange). Any field that travels in JSONL is a compatibility
   question, not a feature question: decide whether this fork must tolerate it
   on import even if it never writes it. `tests/storage_schema_shape.rs` pins
   this fork's serialized field set as a hard external invariant for `bv`, so
   any addition has to go through that test deliberately.

4. **A ranked port list** with one bead filed per accepted item, and an explicit
   rejected list. A comparison that ends in prose and no beads is a comparison
   nobody will act on.

## Constraints

- Read-only against that checkout. Never modify it, never build it into this
  tree, never copy Go source in.
- **Licensing:** the Go original is a separate codebase with its own terms.
  Porting *behaviour* and porting *code* are different acts. Check the Go original's `LICENSE`
  before any line-level borrowing, and record the finding in
  the comparison document — this fork's `NOTICE.md` already tracks lineage and
  will need an entry if anything is taken.
- The Go project is a moving target. Pin the comparison to the commit hash above
  so the document is falsifiable later.

## Sequencing

Do this after `bds-04l.5` (docs, agent surfaces, CI) and `bds-04l.8`
(GoReleaser). Those close out the fork; this opens the next phase. Running it
earlier means comparing against a surface that is still being stripped.

title: Version the JSONL format and give it a migration path
description:
The JSONL interchange format has no version marker and no upgrade path. That is
the real obstacle to changing the data model — not the database.

## Why the DB is not the problem

The SQLite side is already versioned and already migratable:
`CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 15` in `src/storage/schema.rs:10`, stamped into
`PRAGMA user_version`, with `run_pre_schema_migrations` (`:1185`) and
`run_migrations` (`:1315`) executing on open.

More to the point, `.beads/*.db` is **gitignored and derived** — see the
`.gitignore` that `br init` writes. `issues.jsonl` is the source of truth and
the database is a rebuildable cache. Changing a column is already close to free:
worst case, drop the DB and re-import.

So "add a way to change the DB model" is largely already true, and the honest
scope of this task is the format that *is* durable.

## Why JSONL is the problem

A record carries 14 keys — `id, title, description, status, priority,
issue_type, labels, created_at, created_by, updated_at, source_repo,
source_repo_path, compaction_level, original_size` — and **none of them is a
version**. `.beads/metadata.json` is two keys naming files. There is no place to
record which format generation a file was written in, so there is no way to
write an upgrade that runs once and knows it has run.

Two consequences, both live:

- **Adding a field is currently a breaking change with no ramp.**
  `tests/storage_schema_shape.rs` pins the serialized `Issue` field set as a
  hard external invariant because an external viewer parses the file directly.
  That test is correct and should stay strict — but strictness without a
  versioning story means the field set can never move.
- **Reading someone else's JSONL is all-or-nothing.** The Go original's records
  carry fields this fork does not model (see the parity round). Today the only
  options are "model it" or "drop it silently".

## What to build

1. **A format version, written once and read on import.** Decide where it
   lives: a per-record key, a header record, or `metadata.json`. A per-record
   key is the only one that survives concatenation and 3-way merge — this repo
   already ships merge-artifact handling (`beads.{base,left,right}.jsonl`) — but
   it is also the one the pinned field-set test will reject, so that test has to
   be part of the design, not a casualty of it.
2. **An upgrade path keyed on that version**, running on import, idempotent, and
   reporting what it changed. Model it on the existing DB migration gates
   (`user_version < N`), not on the probe-the-table style that sits beside them.
3. **A forward-compatibility rule for unknown keys.** Decide explicitly whether
   an unrecognized field is preserved on round-trip or dropped. Preserving it is
   what makes another tool's file safe to read and write back; dropping it is
   silent data loss and is what happens today by default. Whichever is chosen,
   pin it with a test that round-trips a record containing an unknown key.

## Prior art already in this tree — reuse it, do not reinvent

ID rewriting on import already exists and works: `br sync --rename-prefix` maps
mismatched IDs through `build_prefix_renames` (`src/sync/mod.rs:4515`), detects
collisions in `scan_import_collision_renames`, and applies the result inside
`stream_import_actions_in_tx` with foreign keys disabled and re-validated after.

That is the shape a data-level migration should take. Note what it demonstrates:
rewriting an ID is *not* a schema migration — it fans out into hierarchical
child IDs (which embed the parent ID verbatim), dependency rows, and free text.
Do not fold ID rewriting into the format-version mechanism; they are different
operations that happen to run at the same moment.

## Explicit non-goal

Do not build a general "rename any issue ID" command as part of this. Upstream's
Go implementation has `rename` and `rename-prefix` as first-class commands; let
the parity round (bds-i3g) decide on evidence whether this fork wants them.

## Acceptance criteria

- A JSONL file written by this version records its format generation, and an
  older file is recognized as older rather than assumed current.
- An import of a previous-generation file upgrades it, is idempotent on a second
  run, and says what it changed.
- The unknown-key rule is decided, documented, and pinned by a round-trip test.
- `tests/storage_schema_shape.rs` still pins a field set — the invariant is kept,
  with a deliberate, documented change, not weakened to accommodate this.
- `env -u RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN task check` exits 0, with every `running N tests`
  block paired to exactly one `test result:` line.

title: Render Markdown in the rich display paths
description:
`br show` prints every prose block as literal markdown source — `##` headings, `**bold**`, backticked code — because nothing in the tree renders markdown. `src/format/markdown.rs` is a complete but entirely unwired module; `rich_rust` is already a dependency with its `markdown` feature enabled. Wire it into the rich display paths only: styled markdown where styling is already permitted, byte-identical raw markdown when piped, under `--no-color`, or under `--json`, so `br show <id> | glow -` and agent parsing both keep working.

Architecture: a new `render_markdown_text(content, width) -> Text` in `src/format/markdown.rs` that splits the source into top-level blocks first, then renders each block knowing its kind — prose blocks wrapped here, fixed blocks (tables, fenced code, rules) rendered at exact width and left untouched. Consumed by `IssuePanel` and the two rich paths in `comments.rs`. The compact `format_issue_details` path is deliberately unchanged. The dead `src/format/rich.rs` is deleted rather than taught markdown.

Tech stack: Rust, `rich_rust` 0.2.2 (`markdown` feature, backed by pulldown-cmark), the existing `Text`/`Panel` renderables and `Theme`.
design:
# Render Markdown in the rich display paths

## The bug as reported

`br show` now prints every prose block — description, Design, Acceptance
Criteria, Notes — but prints them as literal markdown source: `##` headings,
`**bold**`, backticked code. The reported question was whether the main body
renders correctly and the other blocks do not.

It does not. **Nothing renders markdown anywhere.** Both display paths emit the
source text:

- `src/cli/commands/show.rs:1194-1237` — description, Design, Acceptance
  Criteria and Notes all pass through `wrap_body(sanitize_terminal_text(…))`,
  which strips control characters and soft-wraps on word boundaries. There is
  no markdown parsing in that path at all.
- `src/output/components/issue_panel.rs:93-100` — the Rich panel applies one
  flat `theme.issue_description` style to the whole description string.

## What already exists, and why it never worked

`src/format/markdown.rs` is a complete, unused module. It defines
`render_markdown` with Rich / Plain / JSON / Quiet behaviour, wrapping
`rich_rust`'s `Markdown` renderable, and `format/mod.rs:68` re-exports it.
**Nothing calls it.** `rich_rust` is already a dependency with the `markdown`
feature enabled (`Cargo.toml:97`), so the crate is in the tree.

This is not a regression. The module arrived unwired in the initial commit and
is equally unwired in the tree this project derives from (see `NOTICE.md`),
where `Markdown::new` likewise appears exactly once — inside the same dead
function — and `render_markdown` likewise has no callers outside its own unit
tests. There is no prior working implementation to restore or copy.

## Why wiring it up naively fails

`rich_rust`'s markdown renderer **styles but does not wrap**, and pads. Measured
directly against `rich_rust` 0.2.2 at width 80:

- A 210-column paragraph came back as a single 210-column line.
- A long list item came back at roughly 103 columns.
- Every *short* line is right-padded with spaces out to the target width.

Headings, emphasis, inline code, blockquotes, task-list checkboxes, GFM tables
and OSC-8 hyperlinks all render correctly. So what is available is a styler,
not a formatter.

That matters because `br show` gained soft-wrapping deliberately (`wrap_body`,
`show.rs:1050-1091`). Passing prose straight through the renderable would
regress it.

Two smaller findings from the same probe:

- Fenced code renders flat grey. `rich_rust`'s code-block path wants its
  `syntax` feature, which `Cargo.toml:94-97` deliberately excludes from the
  release build until the upstream syntect stack drops its unmaintained
  transitive crates.
- `markdown.rs:315` hard-codes `.hyperlinks(true)`, so OSC-8 emission is not
  gated the way colour is.

## Decision: piped output stays raw

Styled markdown is emitted **only where styling is already permitted**. Piped
output, `--no-color`, and `--json` keep byte-identical raw markdown.

This preserves `br show <id> | glow -`, which the agent-facing workflow
recommends, keeps agent parsing stable, and leaves the pinned goldens in
`tests/output_contracts.rs` untouched.

`show.rs:204` already splits exactly this way: Rich mode dispatches to
`IssuePanel`, everything else to the compact `format_issue_details`. **The
compact path therefore needs no changes whatsoever**, and the fact that
`tests/output_contracts.rs` stays green without modification is the cheapest
available proof that the decision held.

The same split holds in `comments.rs`: `:277` is the plain path and is left
alone; `:330` and `:384` are the rich paths.

Consequence worth stating explicitly rather than discovering later:
`br show --no-color` on a terminal resolves to Plain mode, so it too keeps raw
markdown.

## Approach: render per block, not per document

The flat `Vec<Segment>` that `Markdown::render` returns does not say which
output lines are a table row and which are a paragraph, and wrapping a table row
destroys it. Recovering that from styling alone is fragile.

Invert it: **split the source into top-level blocks first, then render each
block knowing its kind.**

New in `src/format/markdown.rs`:

```
render_markdown_text(content: &str, width: usize) -> Text
```

- **Prose blocks** — paragraph, heading, list, blockquote — render at `width`,
  then right-trim and wrap at `width` here, carrying a list item's leading
  indent onto its continuation lines the way `wrap_body` already does.
  Rendering at `width` loses nothing: `rich_rust` does not wrap, so an
  over-long paragraph comes back over-long either way, and the only effect of
  the width argument on prose is the right-padding that gets trimmed anyway.
- **Fixed blocks** — tables, fenced code, horizontal rules — render at exactly
  `width` and keep the renderer's own layout.

`rich_rust` does **not** clamp table width: a table asked for width 30 comes
back at 58 columns on every line. So `render_markdown_text` guarantees the
invariant itself — no emitted line exceeds `width`, with over-wide fixed-block
lines **cropped**. Cropping keeps a table row readable as a row; wrapping turns
it into mush, and an over-wide line breaks the panel border either way.

With that guarantee, the panel's existing `wrap_rich_text`
(`issue_panel.rs:271`) is a no-op on fixed blocks: it only touches over-long
lines. It can therefore stay in place unchanged, and the two wrapping layers do
not fight.

On any renderer error, fall back to the sanitized source text rather than
failing the command.

### The block split needs a parser, not a hand-rolled scanner

Add **`pulldown-cmark`** to `[dependencies]`. It is already in `Cargo.lock` at
0.13.3, pulled in by `rich_rust`'s `markdown` feature, so promoting it to a
direct dependency costs no new compilation — and it makes block classification
exact instead of guessed. The alternative is a hand-rolled markdown scanner,
which is the same fragility this approach exists to avoid.

Use it only to identify top-level blocks and their kinds, then slice the source
and hand each slice to `rich_rust`'s `Markdown::render`. Walking the full AST
and emitting `Text` directly is a larger design that was considered and set
aside; this is the narrow use.

**Caveat the split introduces:** rendering a block in isolation breaks
reference-style links, because `[text][ref]` and its `[ref]: url` definition are
different blocks. Either re-append collected link definitions to each rendered
block, or accept and document the limitation. Pin whichever is chosen with a
test.

### No wrapping crate

Wrapping stays in segment space, in this repo. `rich_rust`'s `Text::wrap` is
already style-preserving — it wraps via `slice()`, which re-maps spans onto the
sliced range (`text.rs:501-531`) — and is already used at
`issue_panel.rs:271`. The only thing it lacks is initial/subsequent indent, and
`wrap_body` (`show.rs:1050-1091`) already implements exactly that. Port that
logic from `&str` to `Text`.

A string-space wrapper such as `textwrap` cannot be used here even though it is
good at the job. `Text::cell_len` sums `unicode_width` per character with no
ANSI skipping (`cells.rs:27-38`): `ESC` measures 0, but the `[31m` after it
measures 4. Feeding a pre-rendered ANSI string back into a `Text` therefore
corrupts every downstream width calculation — panel borders, alignment and
wrapping alike. Every `&str`-in/`&str`-out wrapper forces that round trip.

## Ordering constraint

`sanitize_terminal_text` runs on the **source**, before rendering. The
renderer's own escapes are then the only ANSI present, and a crafted
description cannot inject its own.

Reversing this order would strip the escapes just generated *and* pass source
escapes through — a terminal-injection hole. Pin it with a test that feeds a
description containing a raw escape sequence and asserts it does not survive
into the output.

## Call sites

| Site | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `issue_panel.rs:93` plus the Design / Acceptance Criteria / Notes section and comments | `append_text(&render_markdown_text(…))` in place of `append_styled` |
| `comments.rs:330`, `comments.rs:384` | same |
| `issue_table.rs:279` | inline strip only — reuse the already-written `strip_markdown` (`markdown.rs:63`) |
| `src/format/rich.rs` | delete |
| `src/cli/commands/show.rs`, `comments.rs:277` | unchanged, deliberately |

`issue_table.rs:279` is the `--context` search-snippet cell. It gets stripping,
not styling: that cell's styling is owned by the search-term highlighter
(`highlight_text`), and a second styling pass would fight it. Block elements
cannot fit one table cell in any case.

## Deleting `src/format/rich.rs`

All six public items in that 540-line module have **zero users outside the
file**: `RichIssueTable`, `RichIssuePanel`, `RichDependencyTree`,
`format_status_badge`, `format_count_badges`, `build_completion_bar`. Each is
referenced only by the module's own two unit tests at `rich.rs:420,440`. The
module is kept compiling by nothing but itself, and is equally unused in the
tree this project derives from.

Teaching a dead second panel implementation to render markdown would be work
spent on code no command can reach. Delete the file and drop `pub mod rich;`
from `format/mod.rs`.

## Deliberately out of scope

- `src/format/syntax.rs` is also entirely unused — `highlight_code`,
  `parse_code_fence` and `detect_language_from_filename` have no callers. Leave
  it. It is the natural home for code-fence highlighting in a follow-up,
  precisely because `rich_rust`'s `syntax` feature is excluded from this build.
- `contains_markdown` and `escape_markdown` are unused; let them live or die
  with the implementation rather than making them a separate decision.
- `history.rs:726` prints diffs, and `error/structured.rs` prints error text.
  Neither is markdown.

## Testing

- Unit tests on `render_markdown_text`: a long paragraph wraps at width; a list
  continuation keeps its indent; a table row survives byte-identical; a fenced
  code block is preserved; no line carries trailing padding.
- A panel-level test asserting a rendered `## Heading` contains ANSI and no
  literal `##`.
- A regression test pinning `format_issue_details` output byte-identical to
  today.
- The terminal-injection test described under **Ordering constraint**.
- `tests/output_contracts.rs` must pass **unmodified**. Any edit to that file is
  a signal the piped-output decision was violated.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `br show <id>` on a TTY renders headings, emphasis, inline code, lists, blockquotes, task-list checkboxes and GFM tables for description, Design, Acceptance Criteria and Notes — no literal `##` or `**` reaches the terminal.
- [ ] Comment bodies render the same way in `br comments` and inside the show panel.
- [ ] Long paragraphs and long list items wrap at the panel width; list continuations keep their indent; no prose line carries trailing padding (fixed blocks keep the renderer's own layout).
- [ ] Table rows, fenced code blocks and horizontal rules survive byte-identical — never re-wrapped.
- [ ] Piped output, `--no-color` and `--json` emit byte-identical raw markdown, unchanged from today.
- [ ] `tests/output_contracts.rs` passes unmodified — no edit to that file.
- [ ] `sanitize_terminal_text` runs on the source before rendering; a description containing a raw escape sequence cannot inject ANSI into the output, pinned by a test.
- [ ] A renderer error falls back to the sanitized source text rather than failing the command.
- [ ] `src/format/rich.rs` is deleted and `pub mod rich;` removed from `format/mod.rs`.
- [ ] `env -u RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN task check` exits 0.
notes:
# Global Constraints

Every task's requirements implicitly include this section.

## Toolchain

- **Prefix every `cargo` / `rustc` / `task` invocation with `env -u RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN`.** There is no `rust-toolchain.toml`; a stale exported `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN` silently builds on nightly and still reports success.
- The gate is `env -u RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN task check` and it must exit 0 before any commit. It runs `toolchain:check`, `format:check`, `lint` (clippy over every target), then `test`.
- `rust-version = "1.95"`. Do not use features newer than that.
- Building needs a C compiler — `rusqlite`'s `bundled` feature compiles SQLite from C source.

## Tests

- The suite runs under **cargo-nextest**, one process per test. `task test` runs `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast` **and then** `cargo test --workspace --doc`. Never substitute a bare `cargo nextest run` — nextest cannot run doctests and they would silently stop running.
- Run a subset with `env -u RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN task test:one -- -E 'test(<name>)'`. Nextest selects by filterset, not `--test <binary> <name>`.
- Clippy runs with **pedantic + nursery** (`[lints.clippy]` in `Cargo.toml`). New code must pass without `#[allow]` unless an existing neighbouring pattern already uses one.
- Do not reconcile test counts by arithmetic. Use `cargo nextest list --workspace` before and after and diff the actual names.

## Files that must not change

- **`tests/output_contracts.rs` must pass unmodified.** Any edit to that file means the piped-output decision was violated. It pins the machine-readable goldens consumers parse.
- The compact path `format_issue_details` (`src/cli/commands/show.rs:1094-1282`) and the plain comments path (`src/cli/commands/comments.rs:277`) stay byte-identical. Piped output, `--no-color` and `--json` keep raw markdown.

## Where a new test goes

- Unit tests live in a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` inside the module under test. That is where every test in this plan goes.
- Integration tests are grouped into a handful of binaries; a new file needs both a file in the directory **and** a `#[path]` line in the crate root (`tests/e2e.rs`, `tests/storage.rs`, `tests/proptest.rs`, `tests/repro.rs`). No task in this plan adds one.

## Licensing guard

- `tests/licensing.rs` fails the build if any git-tracked file other than `NOTICE.md` and itself names an upstream project or a path on someone else's machine. Do not write such a sentence in a doc comment, a README section, or a commit message that ends up quoted in a tracked file. Link to `NOTICE.md` instead.
- Never describe this project as plain-MIT-licensed. `Cargo.toml` uses `license-file` because the licence carries a binding rider with no SPDX identifier.
- After staging any new or edited tracked file, run `env -u RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN cargo test --test licensing`.

## Commits

- **Commit messages must parse as Conventional Commits.** `.cliff.toml` builds `CHANGELOG.md` from them and that becomes the release body. Accepted: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `chore`, `build`, `ci`, `test`, `perf`, `style`, `refactor`, `revert`, plus a `!` breaking marker. `plan:` is rejected.
- **Never add AI or agent attribution trailers** — no `Co-Authored-By` naming an assistant, no `Generated with …`, no variant, in any commit, PR body, release note or tag message. Nothing in the gate or the hooks will catch one, and history is not rewritable once pushed.
- Do not skip hooks and do not add `--no-verify`. Install them once with `pre-commit install`.

## The remote

- **Never write to the remote without explicit approval, every time.** No `git push` in any form, no `gh pr` / `gh release` / `gh workflow run`, no `gh api` with a non-GET method, no tag push.
- Reading is fine and needs no approval: `gh pr list`, `gh pr diff`, `gh run view`, `gh api` GETs.
- Local work — committing, branching, resetting — is outside this rule.

title: Add render_markdown_text: block-aware markdown to styled Text
description:
Add `render_markdown_text(content: &str, width: usize) -> Text` to `src/format/markdown.rs`.

Split the markdown source into top-level blocks first, then render each block knowing its kind — because the flat `Vec<Segment>` that `rich_rust`'s `Markdown::render` returns does not say which output lines are a table row and which are a paragraph, and wrapping a table row destroys it.

DEPENDENCY: add `pulldown-cmark` to `[dependencies]`. It is already in `Cargo.lock` at 0.13.3 via `rich_rust`'s `markdown` feature, so promoting it to a direct dependency costs no new compilation. Use it ONLY to identify top-level blocks and their kinds, then slice the source and hand each slice to `Markdown::render`. Walking the full AST and emitting `Text` directly is a larger design that was considered and set aside.

Caveat the split introduces: rendering a block in isolation breaks reference-style links, because `[text][ref]` and its `[ref]: url` definition are different blocks. Either re-append collected link definitions to each rendered block, or accept and document the limitation — pin whichever is chosen with a test.

Prose blocks (paragraph, heading, list, blockquote): render at an effectively unbounded width so rich_rust never right-pads, then wrap at `width` here.

Fixed blocks (tables, fenced code, horizontal rules): render at exactly `width` and leave untouched. Because they come out at exactly `width`, the panel's existing `wrap_rich_text` (issue_panel.rs:271) is a no-op on them — it only touches over-long lines — so the two wrapping layers do not fight.

WRAPPING: no new crate. Stay in segment space. `Text::wrap` is already style-preserving — it wraps via `slice()`, which re-maps spans onto the sliced range (text.rs:501-531) — and is already used at issue_panel.rs:271. It lacks only initial/subsequent indent, which `wrap_body` (show.rs:1050-1091) already implements; port that logic from `&str` to `Text`. A string-space wrapper such as textwrap cannot be used even though it is good at the job: `Text::cell_len` sums unicode_width per character with no ANSI skipping (cells.rs:27-38), so ESC measures 0 but the `[31m` after it measures 4, and feeding pre-rendered ANSI back into a `Text` corrupts panel borders, alignment and wrapping.

On any renderer error, fall back to the sanitized source text rather than failing the command.

Measured baseline against rich_rust 0.2.2 at width 80: a 210-column paragraph came back as one 210-column line, a long list item at ~103 columns, and every short line was right-padded to 80. Headings, emphasis, inline code, blockquotes, task-list checkboxes, GFM tables and OSC-8 hyperlinks all render correctly.

Acceptance criteria:
- A long paragraph wraps at the requested width.
- A list continuation line keeps its parent item's indent.
- A table row survives byte-identical.
- A fenced code block is preserved.
- No prose line carries trailing padding; fixed blocks keep the renderer's own layout.
- Reference-style link behaviour across the block split is pinned by a test.
- A renderer error yields the source text, not a command failure.

title: Wire markdown rendering into IssuePanel
description:
Consume `render_markdown_text` in `src/output/components/issue_panel.rs`, replacing `append_styled` with `append_text` for every prose block: the description (:93-100), the Design / Acceptance Criteria / Notes section, and comment bodies (:262-266).

`show.rs:204` dispatches Rich mode to `IssuePanel` and everything else to the compact path, so this is the change that makes `br show` render markdown on a terminal.

Ordering constraint — `sanitize_terminal_text` runs on the SOURCE, before rendering. The renderer's own escapes are then the only ANSI present, and a crafted description cannot inject its own. Reversing the order would strip the escapes just generated and pass source escapes through, which is a terminal-injection hole.

Leave `wrap_rich_text` (:271) in place — fixed blocks arrive at exactly the content width, so it is a no-op on them.

Acceptance criteria:
- `br show <id>` on a TTY renders headings, emphasis, inline code, lists, blockquotes, task-list checkboxes and GFM tables across description, Design, Acceptance Criteria and Notes.
- No literal `##` or `**` reaches the terminal.
- A panel-level test asserts a rendered `## Heading` contains ANSI and no literal `##`.
- A test feeds a description containing a raw escape sequence and asserts it does not survive into the output.

title: Strip markdown from the --context search snippet
design:
# Task 7: Strip markdown from the `--context` search snippet

**Depends on Task 4** only for `strip_markdown` being `pub(crate)`. Independent
of Tasks 5 and 6.

**Files:**
- Modify: `src/output/components/issue_table.rs:275-285` — the `--context` cell
- Modify: `src/format/markdown.rs` — export `strip_markdown` as `pub(crate)`, drop the `#[allow(dead_code)]` Task 4 left on it
- Modify: `src/output/components/issue_table.rs:338` (`mod tests`) — add one test

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `crate::format::markdown::strip_markdown(content: &str) -> String`
- Produces: `fn plain_snippet(snippet: &str) -> String` — private to `issue_table.rs`

## Why stripping and not styling

This cell is the search-context snippet. Two reasons it must not be styled:

1. The cell's styling is already owned by the query highlighter — the existing
   `highlight_text(sanitized_snippet, highlight_regex, theme)` call immediately
   below. A second styling pass would fight it.
2. Block elements cannot fit in one table cell in any case.

So the goal is only that a snippet reads as clean prose instead of showing `##`
and `**` markers.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

Add to `mod tests` in `src/output/components/issue_table.rs`:

```rust
#[test]
fn plain_snippet_strips_markers_and_flattens_to_one_line() {
    let snippet = "## Heading\n\nSome **bold** and `code` text.";
    let out = plain_snippet(snippet);

    assert!(!out.contains('#'), "got {out:?}");
    assert!(!out.contains('*'), "got {out:?}");
    assert!(!out.contains('\n'), "a table cell must be one line: {out:?}");
    assert!(out.contains("Heading"));
    assert!(out.contains("bold"));
}

#[test]
fn plain_snippet_sanitizes_terminal_escapes() {
    let out = plain_snippet("danger \x1b[2J here");
    assert!(!out.contains('\x1b'), "raw escape survived: {out:?}");
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run it to make sure it fails**

```bash
env -u RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN task test:one -- -E 'test(plain_snippet)'
```

Expected: FAIL — compile error, `cannot find function plain_snippet`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Make `strip_markdown` visible**

In `src/format/markdown.rs`, change:

```rust
fn strip_markdown(content: &str) -> String {
```

to:

```rust
pub(crate) fn strip_markdown(content: &str) -> String {
```

and delete the `#[allow(dead_code)]` Task 4 attached to it.

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the implementation**

In `src/output/components/issue_table.rs`:

```rust
/// Flatten a search snippet for a one-line table cell.
///
/// Stripped rather than rendered: this cell's styling belongs to the query
/// highlighter applied just after, and block elements cannot fit one cell.
fn plain_snippet(snippet: &str) -> String {
    let sanitized = sanitize_terminal_text(snippet);
    crate::format::markdown::strip_markdown(sanitized.as_ref())
        .split_whitespace()
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join(" ")
}
```

`split_whitespace().join(" ")` is what collapses the newlines `strip_markdown`
leaves behind into the single line a table cell needs.

Then replace the cell construction (currently `:275-285`):

```rust
if self.columns.context {
    let snippet = self
        .context_snippets
        .as_ref()
        .and_then(|snippets| snippets.get(&issue.id))
        .map_or("", String::as_str);
    let plain = plain_snippet(snippet);
    let snippet_text = highlight_text(&plain, highlight_regex.as_ref(), self.theme);
    cells.push(Cell::new(snippet_text).style(self.theme.muted.clone()));
}
```

The `sanitize_terminal_text` call moves inside `plain_snippet`, so remove the
now-duplicated `let sanitized_snippet = …` line.

- [ ] **Step 5: Run the tests to verify they pass**

```bash
env -u RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN task test:one -- -E 'test(plain_snippet)'
```

Expected: 2 passed.

- [ ] **Step 6: Check the search path end to end**

```bash
env -u RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN cargo build
./target/debug/br list --context markdown
```

Expected: snippets read as prose, and the search term is still highlighted.

- [ ] **Step 7: Run the gate**

```bash
env -u RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN task check
```

Expected: exits 0, and no `dead_code` warning remains for `strip_markdown`.

- [ ] **Step 8: Verify the licensing guard and commit**

```bash
git add -A
env -u RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN cargo test --test licensing
git commit -m "feat(output): strip markdown from search context snippets"
```

title: Over-wide markdown tables crop to near-nothing in br show
description:
Symptom: in a 100-column terminal, `br show bds-jgk` renders the Call-sites table with the first column at ~86 columns and the second cropped to five characters ("Chang", "appe", "same"). The row structure survives but the content does not.

Repro: `br show bds-jgk` on a 100-column TTY, scroll to the 'Call sites' table in the Design field.

Cause: rich_rust lays a table out at its natural content width and does not clamp to the requested width — a table asked for width 30 comes back at 58. bds-jgk.1.3 added crop-to-width for fixed blocks so an over-wide line cannot break the panel border or be shredded by wrap_rich_text. Cropping preserves row structure, which is why it was chosen over wrapping, but for a table whose natural width far exceeds the panel it discards most of the content.

Expected: an over-wide table should remain readable. Two candidate approaches, neither yet chosen:
1. Fall back to emitting the table's raw markdown source as prose when its rendered width exceeds the target, so every cell is visible and wraps normally. Loses the box drawing, keeps the content.
2. Pre-narrow the table before handing it to rich_rust, or post-process column widths.

Also observed while investigating: inline code inside a table cell is NOT rendered — `issue_panel.rs:93` keeps its literal backticks. That is a rich_rust table-cell limitation, separate from the width problem.

Not a regression: before this epic the whole body printed as raw markdown, so nothing that used to be readable became unreadable. This is a shortfall of the new rendering, not a step backwards.

comments.author: anton
comments.text: Fixed in c4beec4. Rather than either candidate in the description, tables now render through rich_rust's Table renderable, whose render(max_width) is a true maximum: it wraps cell content to fit and leaves a narrower table at its natural size. So the box drawing AND the content both survive. Verified on the original repro (br show bds-jgk at 100 columns): the Call-sites second column is fully readable. The inline-code observation is also fixed incidentally -- cells are flattened from the parser's events, so an Event::Code contributes its text without backticks.

title: Nested fixed blocks are classified as Prose and get shredded
description:
Symptom: a fenced code block inside a list item, or a table inside a blockquote, is wrapped as prose instead of being left alone. Confirmed live on a 40-column pty: a code line inside a numbered list wrapped across three lines, and a blockquoted table came out as `| column alpha | column beta |` / `column gamma |` — exactly the row-shredding the Fixed/crop design exists to prevent.

Cause: `classify_block` (src/format/markdown.rs:80) inspects only the TOP-LEVEL tag. `split_top_level_blocks` emits one block per top-level element, so a List or BlockQuote containing a CodeBlock or Table is classified Prose in its entirety and routed through `wrap_text_with_indent`.

Expected: a fixed sub-element should keep the renderer's layout wherever it appears. Likely needs the splitter to descend into container blocks and emit mixed Prose/Fixed segments, rather than classifying the container as a whole.

Not a regression — before this epic the entire body printed as literal markdown. And 0 of 26 prose fields in this repo's own .beads/issues.jsonl hit it today. But code blocks inside list items are very common markdown, and the corruption is silent.

No test covers nesting: split_top_level_blocks_classifies_each_block asserts top-level only, and split_top_level_blocks_keeps_nested_lists_as_one_block asserts the grouping without exercising its consequence. Any fix must add one.

Found by the epic's final whole-branch review.

comments.author: anton
comments.text: Fixed in c4beec4. split_blocks now descends into containers and lifts each code block and table out, rather than classifying the container whole. Their content comes from the parser's events, not a source slice: pulldown-cmark strips a container's prefix from the nested block's first line only, so the range of a fence inside a blockquote still carries '> ' on every following line. Prose keeps its source slice, so a list's numbering survives the split (rich_rust honours an ordered list's start number). Three tests added at the splitter and two end-to-end, per the note that no test covered nesting. One thing changed beyond the report: lifting nested code out meant it would now be cropped like top-level code, losing content the prose path had preserved, so code lines are broken at the width boundary instead -- every character survives.
